acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a writ petition against the order passed by respondent No.1 - Presiding Officer of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens' Tribunal.

legal_principles.principle: The Tribunal shall have all the powers of a civil court for the purpose of taking evidence on oath and of enforcing the attendance of witnesses.
legal_principles.held: Sub-clause (2) clearly indicates that the Tribunal shall have all the powers of a civil court for the purpose of taking evidence on oath and of enforcing the attendance of witnesses.
applicable_acts_sections: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005 — Section 8

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot evict another from a residential premises without following due process and obtaining a valid order.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that Nalini Shah was not having any right to move the Tribunal and that she was not having any right to evict Sheetal Shah from the residential premises.

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot collude with another to oust a third person from their rightful possession of property.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that Nalini Shah and Devang Shah are acting in collusion with a common intention of causing and ousting Sheetal Shah from her matrimonial house.

outcome.final_order: The court called for records and proceedings from the respondent No.1 and after perusing the legality and propriety of the impugned order, issued a writ of certiorari and/or any other appropriate writ, order or direction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
